issue: Pulumi state: bucket replacement loop. GCP returned 409 'bucket already exists' because Pulumi state had pendingReplacement:true on the bucket resource, location mismatch ('US' vs actual 'EUROPE-WEST3'), and a duplicate api-images registry URN (us-central1 and europe-west3 both in state). Pulumi tried to delete-then-recreate the bucket on every run.
fix: Exported state JSON, removed duplicate us-central1 registry entry, corrected bucket location to EUROPE-WEST3, removed pendingReplacement flag, re-imported state, ran pulumi refresh to sync. Also deleted stale us-central1 Artifact Registry repo from GCP directly.

issue: Cloud Run reserved env var. Pulumi infra/index.ts had PORT=8080 in container envs. Cloud Run injects PORT automatically and rejects any attempt to set it manually: 'Error 400: spec.template.spec.containers[0].env: The following reserved env names were provided: PORT'
fix: Removed { name: 'PORT', value: '8080' } from container envs in infra/index.ts

issue: Same PORT=8080 reserved env var in the gcloud run deploy step inside deploy.yml. The --set-env-vars string included PORT=8080.
fix: Removed PORT=8080 from --set-env-vars in deploy.yml gcloud run deploy step.

issue: Test and Infra jobs passed for first time. Deploy job built and pushed image OK, but container failed to start on Cloud Run. Cloud Run health probe timed out. Cloud Run logs showed: PathError [TypeError]: Missing parameter name at index 1: * at server.ts:67. Express 5 upgraded path-to-regexp to v8 which removed bare * wildcard support.
fix: Changed app.get('*', ...) to app.get('{*path}', ...) in packages/api/src/server.ts to use Express 5 / path-to-regexp v8 compatible syntax.

issue: None. All three jobs passed: Test (36s), Infra (46s), Deploy (1m55s). Cloud Run URL: https://bedtime-api-del75zytpq-ey.a.run.app. API responding with 401 on /api/auth/me (auth guard working correctly).
fix: No fix needed. However discovered immediately after: root URL '/' also returns 401 because app.use(requireAuth) is global middleware placed before static file serving in server.ts. Static files get auth-gated. Fix: scope requireAuth to /api only.

issue: Frontend HTML/CSS/JS unreachable in production. app.use(requireAuth) in server.ts is a global middleware that runs before the static file serving block. Any unauthenticated request to / or any asset path returns 401 before Express even reaches express.static(). The React SPA cannot load without auth, creating a chicken-and-egg problem.
fix: Changed app.use(requireAuth) to app.use('/api', requireAuth) in packages/api/src/server.ts. This scopes auth enforcement to /api/* paths only. /api/auth/* was already registered before this middleware so login endpoints remain public. Static files at /* are now served without auth, which is correct — the SPA handles its own auth state client-side.
